projects.title: Plant Health Monitoring System
projects.summary: LeafAI is a plant health application that classifies plant diseases from leaf images. It combines a fine-tuned MobileNetV2 model with a Flask REST API to make image-based predictions accessible through a web application.
projects.problem: Identifying plant diseases from leaf images requires interpreting visual symptoms. The project explores how computer vision can make this process faster and more accessible through an image-based prediction workflow.
projects.solution: A MobileNetV2 transfer-learning model was fine-tuned with TensorFlow and Keras, then integrated into a Flask REST API that accepts leaf images and returns disease predictions. CNN architectures were compared to guide model selection before integrating the selected model into the application.
projects.contribution: On our six-person senior design project, I was the sole Computer Science student, working with five AI teammates to bring the team’s MobileNetV2 plant disease model into a Flask application. I focused on connecting leaf-image input, model inference, and the prediction shown to the user.
projects.keyFeature: Image-based plant disease classification through a REST endpoint, connecting the trained computer vision model to an application workflow.
projects.technicalChallenge: Selecting a CNN architecture for plant disease classification and taking the model from training experiments to inference within a Flask application.
highlights: Fine-tuned a MobileNetV2 transfer-learning model for plant disease classification
Compared CNN architectures to guide model selection and reduce experimentation time
Delivered a REST endpoint for real-time prediction from leaf images

projects.title: AURAK's Dine Ordering System
projects.contribution: Contributed to full-stack development as part of a six-person team, including menu management interfaces and connecting the application to its backend and database.
projects.keyFeature: Cafeteria pre-ordering with Stripe checkout and role-based tools for staff to manage menu listings and product images.
projects.technicalChallenge: Connecting the React frontend, Express backend, and PostgreSQL database, then configuring the application to run on Render with a Neon-hosted database.
projects.summary: A cafeteria pre-ordering website built by a six-person team, with online payments through Stripe and menu management tools for staff.
projects.problem: Students need a convenient way to place cafeteria orders in advance, while staff need a simple way to keep menu listings and product images up to date.
projects.solution: Built a React frontend connected to a Node.js and Express backend with PostgreSQL. The application brings together pre-ordering, Stripe checkout, and role-based menu management, with deployment on Render and database hosting on Neon.
highlights: Stripe-based checkout was included in the team’s ordering workflow.
Built role-based CMS interfaces for menu listings and product images
Automated deployment with render.yaml and a serverless Neon PostgreSQL database

projects.title: Personal Portfolio
projects.summary: A personal website to share my software projects, experience, and photography in one place.
projects.problem: I wanted a simple way to present my technical work and photography, with content I could easily update.
projects.solution: Built a responsive Next.js website with separate sections for software projects and photography. Content is stored in JSON files and updated through local admin tools, and the site is deployed on Vercel.
projects.contribution: Built the project and photography pages, organized the content, and added local tools to update text and images.
projects.keyFeature: Software projects and a photography gallery in one responsive website.
projects.technicalChallenge: Keeping photo-heavy pages fast and making the layout work well on desktop and mobile.
highlights: Separate sections for software projects and photography
Optimized photos and thumbnails for the gallery
